questions.question: How should I proceed from here?

options.label: Merge + register (shadow)
options.description: Run close-work to commit + merge this branch to main, then register the PreToolUse hook globally in shadow mode, static-only first (PERM_GATE_ENFORCE=0, PERM_GATE_CONSULT_AI=0) — zero latency/cost, just logs to perm-gate-decisions.jsonl so you can review verdicts before trusting them.

options.label: Merge only, don't register
options.description: Commit + merge to main so the code is landed and importable, but leave ~/.claude/settings.json untouched — you'll add the hook yourself when ready.

options.label: Hold for review
options.description: Leave everything in this worktree, uncommitted, so you can read the code and the static allow/deny/ask lists before anything lands or registers.

transcript_tail.text: Now run the new tests, then the full suite to confirm no regressions.
All 33 green. Now the full suite + a live smoke test of the hook entrypoint end-to-end.
Hook entrypoint works end-to-end. The full-suite tail got swamped by `test_work_start`'s stdout — let me get the clean summary.

**427 tests pass.** The gate is built and working end-to-end:
- `git status` → `static-allow` (shadow: emits nothing, just logs)
- `rm -rf /` → `static-deny`, `git push origin main` → `static-ask` (enforce: emits the structured decision)
- All exit 0 (never blocks via exit code); decisions logged to JSONL.

Let me write the design/runbook doc the module references, then I'll stop before touching your global settings.

Key finding for registration: `python3 -m remote_control` resolves globally to the **main checkout** (`~/dev/ai-harness`), not this worktree. So a global hook would run main's code — meaning **the code must land in `main` before the hook is registered** (otherwise `perm-gate` is an unknown subcommand there). That sequences the rollout. Let me write the runbook doc.

Core implementation is **done and green**. Summary of what landed in this worktree:

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `remote_control/perm_gate.py` | tiered gate — static rules → AI tier (urllib `/v1/messages`, injectable), fail-safe to `ask`, shadow/enforce, recursion guard |
| `remote_control/config.py` | `PermGateConfig` (shadow by default) |
| `remote_control/cli.py` | `perm-gate` subcommand |
| `tests/test_perm_gate.py` | 33 tests |
| `docs/perm-gate.md` | design + runbook + the settings snippet |

**427 tests pass**, and the hook works end-to-end (verified `allow`/`deny`/`ask` + JSONL logging + always-exit-0). It reuses the manager's `session-manager-cases.md` as the shared policy — closing #22's "Permission prompts TBD" branch.

The one remaining task — **registering the global hook** — has a hard dependency I found: `python3 -m remote_control` resolves to the **main checkout**, so the code must be in `main` before the hook can be registered, and registering touches your live global settings (every session). So that's a deliberate step I won't take without your call.
